stage1/review/A1/v0/Clarity:
Review: The problem identifies the exact component (segmentation adapters and their seg_loss), the change (image-level multiple-instance objective, primary operator top-k mean, masks discarded, all five source datasets), the comparison (mask- versus image-label-supervised MVFA under identical model selection) and the outcomes (pixel AUROC, PRO, image AUROC on the held-out modality).
Feedback: State k (or the fraction of patches) for the top-k operator and whether the image-level loss is applied at all four levels or only at the deepest; otherwise the problem is very well delimited.

stage1/review/A1/v0/Relevance:
Review: Mask dependence of localisation is one of the most consequential limitations of the target paper for clinical use, and the corrected description (masks from only three datasets) makes the relevance concrete. It connects directly to the annotation-efficiency theme of MedicalCLIP, MedCLIP-SAMv2 and MadCLIP.
Feedback: None of substance; mention the weak-supervision setting of MedCLIP-SAMv2 as the closest related contrast.
Rating (1-5): 5
stage1/review/A1/v0/Originality:
Review: Weakly supervised localisation from image labels is an established idea, and MVFA already applies an image-level (mean-pooled) BCE to the patch map of its detection branch. The new element is narrower: supervising the segmentation branch's text-anchored, multi-level patch maps through MIL and testing whether that localisation transfers to unseen modalities. This is a moderately original combination.
Feedback: Make the distinctive hypothesis explicit, e.g. that text-anchored patch similarities allow MIL localisation to transfer across modalities better than visual-only weak supervision, or that the localisation emerges at specific levels.
Rating (1-5): 3
stage1/review/A1/v0/Feasibility:
Review: Requires replacing one loss term in train_zero.py; BMAD provides image labels for all datasets; compute equals MVFA's original training on one GPU; the protocol's validation-based model selection is easy to add.
Feedback: Run a single-fold pilot to rule out degenerate all-zero maps before the full multi-seed study.

stage1/review/A1/v0/Significance:
